epistemic_model.uncertainty_policy: Unobserved surface properties are deterministic scenario priors for reproducible RL experiments, not measured facts.

atmosphere.composition_notes: N2-CO2 dominated. Quiet M dwarf = good atmospheric retention. Trace O2 from photolysis. Mean molecular weight ~0.032 kg/mol.
atmosphere.notes: Ross 128 is one of the quietest M dwarfs known. This makes atmospheric retention more probable. Moderate pressure atmosphere.

geology.bulk_composition: Iron-rich core (possibly larger proportional core than Earth due to elevated Fe/Si ratio), silicate mantle with olivine and pyroxene
geology.tectonic_activity: Low — old planet (9.45 Gyr), likely cooled mantle, minimal plate tectonics. Possible ancient volcanic calderas.
geology.volcanism: Extinct or very rare — localized geothermal remnants possible

flare_profile.notes: Ross 128 is remarkably quiet for an M dwarf. Near-zero flare activity makes this the most radiation-safe planet in the set. The primary challenge is the long day/night cycle (9.86 Earth days), not radiation.

radiation_system.basis: The modeled 0.8 atm atmosphere attenuates the quiet M-dwarf particle environment, but atmospheric column and magnetic shielding are unobserved; this is a conservative mission prior.

biomes.name: Mineral Highlands
biomes.description: Elevated terrain exposing ancient igneous and metamorphic rock formations. Billions of years of geological quiescence have left mineral veins intact and accessible near the surface. Iron-rich with oxidized surface giving a reddish-brown color. Wind-sculpted ridges and exposed cliff faces.

biomes.name: Temperate Plains
biomes.description: Wide, relatively flat terrain with a thin layer of weathered regolith over carbonate-rich bedrock. The most hospitable biome — temperatures are manageable during the long day, and the open terrain allows efficient movement. Scattered clay deposits suggest ancient water activity. Primary landing zone.

biomes.name: Frozen Valleys
biomes.description: Deep topographic depressions where cold air pools during the 118-hour night. Water ice accumulates in these natural cold traps — the primary water source on this planet. Walls of the valleys expose layered sedimentary rock with carbonate mineral veins.

biomes.name: Ancient Volcanic Vents
biomes.description: Remnants of extinct volcanic systems. Dark basaltic rock surrounds collapsed calderas and fumarolic vents that still emit trace sulfurous gases from residual geothermal heat. Ancient hydrothermal circulation locally deposited copper-iron sulfides such as chalcopyrite; titanium and aluminium remain primarily bound in common silicate and oxide minerals.

biomes.name: Ice Fields
biomes.description: Polar and permanently shaded regions where thick water ice deposits have accumulated over geological time. The ice is relatively pure H2O with embedded silicate dust. Surface is treacherous — smooth ice with hidden fissures. The largest water reserve on the planet.

resource_modifiers.notes: Most resource-abundant planet in the set. Resources distributed across biomes but not concentrated in lethal zones. The main challenge is logistics and the 9.86-day rotation creating long, cold nights.
